findings.title: join() can skip terminating some flusher processes when timeout expires
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join iterates over multiple flusher processes and breaks out of the loop as soon as the remaining deadline is <= 0. If the deadline is reached before later processes are visited, those processes are never terminated. Also, `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None` treats timeout == 0 as no deadline, so join can block indefinitely. During shutdown or rebalance this can leave flusher processes running or hang the consumer.

findings.title: Restart path kills unhealthy process but never ensures it has exited
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive calls process.kill() for an unhealthy process and immediately creates a replacement without joining or otherwise verifying the old process has exited. The old process object is replaced, which can leak zombie/process resources. If the old worker is not actually dead (or in the thread-based test mode, where threads cannot be killed), two workers may flush the same shards concurrently, risking duplicate Kafka production and confusing buffer state.

findings.title: Unvalidated --flusher-processes value can crash or silently change behavior
findings.body: The new --flusher-processes option accepts any integer. A negative value reaches SpanFlusher, where num_processes becomes negative and process_to_shards_map is empty; the subsequent shard assignment then raises KeyError during consumer startup. A value of 0 is silently treated as “use one process per assigned shard” because of `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. The option should validate the allowed range or document the sentinel behavior.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag key: shards vs shard
findings.body: The wait_produce timer is tagged with `shards`, while the produce timer and segment_size_bytes metric use `shard`. This inconsistency will make metrics harder to query and can silently break dashboards/alerts that expect a single tag name for flusher shard attribution.

findings.title: Docstring overstates one-process-per-shard behavior
findings.body: The class docstring says the flusher creates one process per shard, but the implementation creates min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards)) processes and may assign multiple shards to one process. The CLI default is also 1 process, so the documented behavior does not match the default or the configurable behavior.
